Al-Baghawi, *Ma'alim al-Tanzil* (Commentary), on Surah 41, verses 6–8:

﴿Say: I am only a man like you.﴾ He means: like one of you. ﴿Only that it has been revealed to me that your God is one God.﴾ This is His saying: ﴿It is revealed to me that your God is one God.﴾ Al-Hasan said: Allah taught him humility. ﴿So take a straight course to Him﴾: turn toward Him in obedience and do not deviate from His path. ﴿And seek His forgiveness﴾ for your sins. ﴿And woe to the polytheists.﴾

﴿Those who do not give zakat (obligatory alms)﴾: Ibn Abbas said: those who do not say "There is no god but Allah".[[Al-Suyuti mentioned in *al-Durr al-Manthur* (7/313), from Ibn Abbas, who said: "They do not testify that there is no god but Allah," and he attributed this to Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi in *al-Asma' wa al-Sifat*.]] This is the zakat of the souls, and the meaning is: they do not purify themselves from shirk (association of partners with Allah) through tawhid (affirmation of Allah's oneness). Al-Hasan and Qatada said: they do not acknowledge zakat, and they do not regard giving it as obligatory. It was said: "Zakat is the bridge of Islam; whoever crosses it is saved, and whoever lags behind it is destroyed."[[Al-Suyuti attributed this in *al-Durr al-Manthur* (7/313) to Abd al-Razzaq and Abd ibn Humayd, from Qatada, with the wording: "Zakat is the bridge of Islam. Whoever crosses it is free and saved, and whoever does not cross it is destroyed."]] Al-Dahhak and Muqatil said: they do not spend in obedience and do not give charity. Mujahid said: they do not purify their deeds. ﴿And they, in the Hereafter, they are disbelievers.﴾

**The Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 41, verses 9–11:**

His saying, may He be exalted and glorified: ﴿Say: Do you indeed disbelieve in the One who created the earth in two days?﴾ — the two days being Sunday and Monday — ﴿and set up rivals to Him? That is the Lord of the worlds.﴾

﴿And He placed within it﴾, meaning in the earth, ﴿firm mountains﴾, meaning fixed mountains, ﴿from above it﴾, meaning from above the earth, ﴿and blessed it﴾, meaning in the earth, through what He created in it of seas, rivers, trees and fruits, ﴿and measured in it its sustenance﴾. Al-Hasan and Muqatil said: He apportioned in the earth the provisions of the servants and the beasts. Ikrimah and al-Dahhak said: He determined in each land what He did not place in another, so that some of them might live by means of others through trade from one land to another. [[See: al-Qurtubi: 15/342–343.]] Al-Kalbi said: He determined bread for the people of one region, dates for the people of another region, millet for the people of another region, and fish for the people of another region, and likewise its sustenance.

﴿In four days﴾ — he means the creation of what is in the earth and the measuring of its sustenance — two days being Tuesday and Wednesday. Together with Sunday and Monday these make four days. He returned the latter to the former in the mention, as you would say: "I married a woman yesterday, and two today," one of them being the one you married yesterday. ﴿Equally for those who ask﴾. Abu Ja'far read "sawa'un" with a raised vowel (raf') as a beginning (mubtada'), meaning: "it is equal." Ya'qub read it in the genitive (jarr) as a qualifier of His saying "in four days." The others read "sawa'an" in the accusative (nasb) as a verbal noun (masdar), meaning: "they became equal," i.e., "equality" (istiwa'), and its meaning is: equally for those who ask about that. Qatadah and al-Suddi said: whoever asks about it, the matter is thus, equal, without addition or subtraction, as an answer to one who asks: "In how many days were the earth and the sustenances created?"

﴿Then He turned to the heaven﴾, meaning He resolved upon creating the heaven, ﴿while it was smoke﴾. That smoke was the vapour of water. ﴿So He said to it and to the earth: Come, willingly or unwillingly.﴾ Meaning: come to what I command you, i.e., do it, just as one says: "Come to what is best," meaning: do it.

Tawus related from Ibn 'Abbas: "Come" means "give." That is, bring forth what I have created in you of benefits for the welfare of the servants.

[Ibn 'Abbas said:] God, may He be exalted and glorified, said: As for you, O heaven, bring forth your sun, your moon and your stars; and as for you, O earth, split open your rivers and bring forth your fruits and your plants. He said to both of them: Do what I command you willingly, or else I will compel you to that [until you do it unwillingly]. So they answered with willingness. [[See al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/316–317; al-Qurtubi: 15/343–344.]] And ﴿They said: We come willingly﴾ [and he did not say "willing (feminine dual)"], because He treated them as the heavens, the earth and those within them; its figurative sense is: "We come with what is in us, willingly." So when He described them with speech, He applied to them in the plural the form of those who have intellect.

Al-Hasan and Muqatil said: He apportioned in the earth the provisions of the servants and the beasts. Ikrimah and al-Dahhak said: He determined in each land what He did not place in another, so that some of them might live by means of others through trade from one land to another. [[See: al-Qurtubi: 15/342–343.]] Al-Kalbi said: He determined bread for the people of one region, dates for the people of another region, millet for the people of another region, and fish for the people of another region, and likewise its sustenance.

﴿In four days﴾ — he means the creation of what is in the earth and the measuring of its sustenance — two days being Tuesday and Wednesday. Together with Sunday and Monday these make four days. He returned the latter to the former in the mention, as you would say: "I married a woman yesterday, and two today," one of them being the one you married yesterday. ﴿Equally for those who ask﴾. Abu Ja'far read "sawa'un" with a raised vowel (raf') as a beginning (mubtada'), meaning: "it is equal." Ya'qub read it in the genitive (jarr) as a qualifier of His saying "in four days." The others read "sawa'an" in the accusative (nasb) as a verbal noun (masdar), meaning: "they became equal," i.e., "equality" (istiwa'), and its meaning is: equally for those who ask about that. Qatadah and al-Suddi said: whoever asks about it, the matter is thus, equal, without addition or subtraction, as an answer to one who asks: "In how many days were the earth and the sustenances created?"

﴿Then He turned to the heaven﴾, meaning He resolved upon creating the heaven, ﴿while it was smoke﴾. That smoke was the vapour of water. ﴿So He said to it and to the earth: Come, willingly or unwillingly.﴾ Meaning: come to what I command you, i.e., do it, just as one says: "Come to what is best," meaning: do it.

Tawus related from Ibn 'Abbas: "Come" means "give." That is, bring forth what I have created in you of benefits for the welfare of the servants.

[Ibn 'Abbas said:] God, may He be exalted and glorified, said: As for you, O heaven, bring forth your sun, your moon and your stars; and as for you, O earth, split open your rivers and bring forth your fruits and your plants. He said to both of them: Do what I command you willingly, or else I will compel you to that [until you do it unwillingly]. So they answered with willingness. [[See al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/316–317; al-Qurtubi: 15/343–344.]] And ﴿They said: We come willingly﴾ [and he did not say "willing (feminine dual)"], because He treated them as the heavens, the earth and those within them; its figurative sense is: "We come with what is in us, willingly." So when He described them with speech, He applied to them in the plural the form of those who have intellect.

﴿So He completed them as seven heavens in two days﴾, that is, He perfected them and finished creating them. ﴿And He revealed in each heaven its command﴾. Ata' related from Ibn 'Abbas: He created in each heaven its creation of angels, and what is in it of seas, mountains of hail, and what none knows except Allah.

Qatadah and al-Suddi said: It means He created in them their sun, their moon, and their stars.

Muqatil said: He revealed to each heaven what He willed of commands and prohibitions, and that was on Thursday and Friday.

﴿And We adorned the lowest heaven with lamps﴾, meaning stars, ﴿and as a protection﴾ for it. "Ḥifẓan" (as a protection) is in the accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun), meaning: We protected it with the stars as a protection from the devils who eavesdrop. ﴿That is﴾ what has been mentioned of His making, ﴿the decree of the Mighty﴾ in His dominion, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ in His protection [[In MS "ب": "by His creation."]].

His saying, Exalted and Majestic is He: ﴿But if they turn away﴾, meaning: these polytheists, from faith after this explanation, ﴿then say: I have warned you﴾, I have frightened you, ﴿of a thunderbolt like the thunderbolt of 'Ad and Thamud﴾, that is, a destruction like their destruction. The "ṣā'iqah" (thunderbolt) is the destroying punishment of anything.

﴿When the messengers came to them﴾, meaning 'Ad and Thamud, ﴿from before them and from behind them﴾. By His saying "from before them" He meant the messengers who were sent to their fathers before them, and by "from behind them" He meant: after the messengers who were sent to their fathers, those who were sent to them, Hud and Salih. So the pronoun in "from before them" refers to 'Ad and Thamud, and in "from behind them" refers to the messengers [[In MS "أ": "the messengers."]] [[Omitted in MS "أ".]]. ﴿That not﴾, meaning, that not ﴿you worship except Allah﴾. ﴿They said: If our Lord had willed, He would have sent down﴾, instead of these messengers, ﴿angels﴾. Abu Sa'id al-Shurayhi informed us: Abu Ishaq al-Tha'labi informed us: 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid al-Isfahani narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya al-'Ubaydi narrated to us: Ahmad ibn Majdah ibn al-Uryan informed us: al-Himmani narrated to us: Ibn Fudayl narrated to us, from al-Ajlah, from al-Dhayyal ibn Harmalah, from Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah, who said: The chiefs of Quraysh and Abu Jahl said: The matter of Muhammad has become confused for us. 'Utbah ibn Rabi'ah said: By Allah, I have heard poetry, soothsaying and magic, and I know something of that, and it is not hidden from me whether he is like that or not. Why do you revile our gods, and mislead our fathers? If you want leadership, we will make you our leader as long as you live. **Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 41, verses 23–27:**

Allah's words: ﴿And that was your assumption which you assumed about your Lord; it has destroyed you﴾, meaning it has ruined you. That is, your assumption that Allah does not know much of what you do has destroyed you. Ibn 'Abbas said: it cast you into the Fire. ﴿So you have become among the losers﴾. Then He informed about their condition, saying:

﴿So if they endure, the Fire is their abode﴾, meaning their dwelling place. ﴿And if they ask to be reconciled﴾, meaning they seek to please Allah and request al-'utba (reconciliation, restored favor), ﴿they will not be among those who are granted reconciliation﴾, meaning those who are pleased. Al-mu'tab is the one whose rebuke is accepted and whose request is granted. It is said: a'tabani fulan, meaning he pleased me after having angered me, and = is'tatabtuhu, meaning I asked him to be pleased, that is, to be content.

﴿And We appointed for them﴾, meaning We sent and entrusted; Muqatil said: We prepared. Al-Zajjaj said: We made them a cause.

﴿Companions﴾, meaning peers from the devils, until they led them astray. ﴿So they made attractive to them what was before them﴾, meaning the affairs of this world, until they preferred it over the Hereafter. ﴿And what was behind them﴾, meaning the affairs of the Hereafter, so they called them to deny it and to reject the Resurrection. ﴿And the word has come into effect against them, among nations﴾ [with nations] [[Addition from "B".]].

﴿Those that passed away before them of jinn and mankind. Indeed, they were losers.﴾

﴿And those who disbelieved said﴾, from the polytheists of Quraysh: ﴿Do not listen to this Qur'an, and make noise during it﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: that means, talk over it (i.e., drown it out with noise). Some of them would advise others: when you see Muhammad reciting, confront him with rajaz (a meter of Arabic verse) and poetry and idle talk. Mujahid said: make noise during it with whistling and clapping. Al-Dahhak said: talk a lot, so that what he says becomes confused for him. Al-Suddi said: shout in his face.

﴿That perhaps you will overcome﴾ Muhammad in his recitation.

﴿So We will surely make those who disbelieved taste a severe punishment, and We will surely recompense them with the worst of what﴾, meaning with the worst of what, that is, with the most ugly of what, ﴿they used to do﴾ in the world, and that is shirk (associating partners with Allah).

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 41, verse 35–40:

﴿And none is granted it except those who are patient﴾: none receives this quality, which is repelling evil with good, ﴿except those who are patient﴾ in restraining anger and bearing what is disliked. ﴿And none is granted it except one of great fortune﴾ in goodness and reward. Qatadah said: "The great fortune" is Paradise, meaning: none receives it except the one for whom Paradise is obligatory.

﴿And if an evil suggestion from Satan should tempt you, then seek refuge in Allah. Indeed, He is the All-Hearing﴾ of your seeking refuge and your words, ﴿the All-Knowing﴾ of your deeds and your states.

His, the Mighty and Majestic, saying: ﴿And of His signs are the night and the day, and the sun and the moon. Do not prostrate to the sun or to the moon, but prostrate to Allah, who created them﴾. He said "khalaqahunna" (who created them) in the feminine because He treated them according to the manner of broken plurals (jam' al-taksir), and He did not treat them according to the manner of giving precedence to the masculine over the feminine (al-taghlib). ﴿If you are truly those who worship Him﴾.

﴿But if they are arrogant﴾ regarding prostration, ﴿then those who are with your Lord﴾, meaning the angels, ﴿glorify Him night and day, and they never tire﴾, meaning they do not grow weary and do not slacken.

﴿And of His signs﴾, the evidences of His power, ﴿is that you see the earth barren﴾, dry and dusty, with no vegetation in it, ﴿but when We send down water upon it, it stirs and swells. Indeed, He who revives it is surely the Reviver of the dead. Indeed, He is over all things Competent﴾.

﴿Indeed, those who deviate concerning Our signs﴾, who incline away from the truth regarding Our proofs. Mujahid said: "They deviate concerning Our signs" by whistling, clapping, idle talk, and noisy clamor. Qatadah said: they lie concerning Our signs. As-Suddi said: they oppose and contend.

Muqatil said: it was revealed concerning Abu Jahl. [[See: al-Qurtubi: 15/366.]]

﴿They are not hidden from Us. Is one who is thrown into the Fire better, or one who comes secure on the Day of Resurrection?﴾ It is said the one thrown into the Fire is Abu Jahl. ﴿It is said the one who comes secure is Hamzah. It was also said: Uthman. And it was said: Ammar ibn Yasir.

﴿Do whatever you wish﴾, a command of threat and warning, ﴿indeed, He is Seeing of what you do﴾, Knowing, and He will recompense you for it.

**Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on Surah 41, verses 41–44:**

﴿Indeed, those who disbelieve in the Reminder﴾ — meaning the Qur'an [[Addition from "B".]] — ﴿when it came to them﴾. Then he proceeded to describe the Reminder and left out the response to "Indeed, those who disbelieve," with the implied meaning: "Those who disbelieve in the Reminder will be recompensed for their disbelief." It was also said that its predicate is his statement that follows: "They are called from a distant place."

﴿And indeed it is a Book of might﴾. Al-Kalbi related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, that it means: noble with Allah. Qatada said: Allah has made it mighty with a might such that falsehood finds no path to it [[See: al-Durr al-Manthur: 7/332.]].

This is His statement: ﴿Falsehood cannot approach it from before it or from behind it﴾. Qatada and al-Suddi said: "Falsehood" is Satan; he is unable to alter it, add to it, or subtract from it [[See: al-Tabari: 24/125.]].

Al-Zajjaj said: The meaning is that it is protected from having anything subtracted from it, so that falsehood would come to it "from before it," or from having anything added to it, so that falsehood would come to it "from behind it." On this view, the meaning of "falsehood" is addition and subtraction.

Muqatil said: Denial from the earlier books cannot reach it, and no book will come after it to nullify it.

﴿A revelation from the All-Wise, the Praiseworthy﴾.

Then Allah consoled His Prophet ﷺ regarding their denial.

He said: ﴿What is said to you﴾ of harm, ﴿is only what was said to the messengers before you﴾. He means: It was said to the prophets and messengers before you, "He is a sorcerer," just as it is said to you, and they were denied just as you were denied. ﴿Indeed, your Lord is Forgiving﴾ to those who repent and believe in you, ﴿and Possessor of painful punishment﴾ for those who persist in denial.

﴿And if We had made it﴾ — that is, if We had made this Book which you recite to the people — ﴿a non-Arabic Qur'an﴾, in a language other than the language of the Arabs, ﴿they would have said: "Why have its verses not been explained?"﴾ That is, "Why have its verses not been clarified in Arabic so that we may understand them?" ﴿What! A non-Arabic [Book] and an Arab [Messenger]?﴾ meaning: "A non-Arabic Book and an Arab Messenger?" This is an interrogative in the form of denial, meaning that they used to say: "The one to whom it was revealed is Arab, and the revelation is non-Arabic."

Muqatil said: The reason for this is that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to visit Yasar, the slave of 'Amir ibn al-Hadrami, who was a non-Arab Jew, known by the kunya Abu Fukayha. The polytheists said: "Only Yasar teaches him." His master beat him and said: "You are teaching Muhammad." Yasar said: "Rather, he is teaching me." Then Allah the Exalted revealed this verse [[See what preceded in the tafsir of Surah al-Nahl: 5/44–45.]]:

﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad: ﴿It﴾ — meaning the Qur'an — ﴿is for those who believe a guidance and a healing﴾ — guidance from misguidance and healing for what is in the hearts. It was also said: healing from ailments.

[114/a]

﴿And as for those who do not believe, there is deafness in their ears, and it is blindness for them﴾. Qatada said: They are blind to the Qur'an and deaf to it, so they do not benefit from it. ﴿Those are being called from a distant place﴾. That is, they do not hear and do not understand, just as one who is called from a distant place does not hear and does not understand. This is an example of how little they benefit from what they are admonished with; it is as though they are being called from a place where they cannot hear.

﴿And in themselves﴾: through affliction and sicknesses.

Qatadah said: "in the horizons" means the events of Allah among the nations, and "in themselves" means the Day of Badr.

Mujahid, al-Hasan, and al-Suddi said: "in the horizons" refers to what was conquered of the towns for Muhammad ﷺ and the Muslims, and "in themselves" refers to the conquest of Makkah. [[See: Ibn Kathir in his Tafsir: 4/106.]]

ʿAtaʾ and Ibn Zayd said: "in the horizons" means the regions of the heavens and the earth: the sun, the moon, the stars, the plants, the trees, and the rivers, and "in themselves" means the subtle craftsmanship and wondrous wisdom, until it becomes clear to them that it is the truth. [[See: al-Qurtubi: 15/374–375.]]

﴿Unquestionably, they are in doubt about the meeting with their Lord﴾, in doubt about the Resurrection. ﴿Unquestionably, He encompasses all things in knowledge.﴾
